column1: CX - Android - Fix build and test duration in actions
column33:
We currently have a GitHub Action that triggers when any pull request is opened. For PRs targeting the {{develop}} branch, the build and test job is very delayed, which unnecessarily consumes CI resources and slows feedback.

Update the GitHub Actions workflow so that the build and test process only runs when:

* The pull request’s target (base) branch is {{main}}, *and*
* The pull request has the {{sync-to-release}} label applied.

All other PRs (including those targeting {{develop}} or {{main}} without the label) should *not* run the build/test job.

----

*Acceptance criteria*

* -GitHub Action build/test job runs *only* for PRs whose base branch is {{main}} *and* that have the {{sync-to-release}} label.-
* -PRs targeting {{develop}} (or any non‑{{main}} branch) do *not* trigger the build/test job.-
* -PRs targeting {{main}} without the {{sync-to-release}} label do *not* run the build/test job, and the workflow clearly logs/skips with a reason (e.g. “skipped: missing sync-to-release label or base branch != main”).-
* -Behavior is verified using at least two test PRs (one that matches the conditions and one that doesn’t), and the results are documented in this Jira issue.-

column1: CX - Create a confluence page about the planning of Loggin and catching
column33:
Create a Confluence page that clearly documents the proposed approach for implementing a new logging and try/catch error-handling system in the CreditorX backend. The page should help the team understand the objective, implementation strategy, standards to follow, and criteria for adopting the new approach.

h3. Objective

Define a consistent and maintainable logging and exception-handling strategy for backend services in CreditorX, improving observability, troubleshooting, and error management across the application.

h3. Scope

* Document the recommended logging levels, message structure, and required context for backend logs.
* Explain where and how try/catch blocks should be implemented.
* Define how exceptions should be handled, wrapped, rethrown, or returned to callers.
* Include examples for common backend scenarios, such as service calls, external integrations, validations, and unexpected errors.
* Describe any standards, conventions, or libraries that should be used.

h3. Key sections to include

* Current problem or motivation
* Proposed logging strategy
* Proposed try/catch and error-handling strategy
* Implementation examples
* Best practices and anti-patterns
* Rollout or adoption plan
* Open questions or decisions needed

h3. Out of scope

* Implementing the logging or error-handling changes in code as part of this task.
* Refactoring existing backend modules unless needed as examples.
* Configuring monitoring dashboards or alerts.

h3. Completion criteria

* A Confluence page is created and linked to this task.
* The page explains the recommended logging and try/catch approach clearly and concisely.
* The page includes practical backend examples for CreditorX.
* The content is reviewed with the team and updated with any agreed changes.

column1: CX - Improve exception handler in kazoo api
column33:
Kazoo API errors are currently handled as generic *Internal Server Error* responses, which makes troubleshooting harder and does not clearly communicate known upstream failure scenarios. This task will introduce custom exception handling for Kazoo API failures so the application can map known upstream error cases to the appropriate exception type and HTTP status code instead of defaulting to a generic 500 response.

The implementation should also improve exception messages so they are specific, actionable, and safe. Messages should include useful context such as the Kazoo operation being executed and a correlation or request identifier when available, while avoiding sensitive data such as credentials, tokens, payload secrets, or personally identifiable information.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -A custom Kazoo API exception type, or a small hierarchy of Kazoo-specific exceptions, exists and is used when handling Kazoo API failures.-
* -Known Kazoo upstream error cases are mapped to appropriate exceptions and status codes instead of always returning a generic 500 Internal Server Error.-
* -Exception messages include actionable context such as the operation name and correlation/request ID when available, without exposing secrets or sensitive data.-
* -Automated tests and/or observability updates confirm the new exception mapping, message content, and logging behavior for successful and failing Kazoo API scenarios.-

column1: CP - GraphQL Error Responses
column33:
*Description* 

Make a failing GraphQL operation return an error the frontend can act on, and stop sending internal detail to the client. Operations that fail unexpectedly return no error key today, leaving the frontend with nothing to map to a message, and in production the response includes the stack trace, internal endpoints and customer identifiers. Returning the error key also corrects the log level of these failures, which are recorded as server errors even when the outcome is expected.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* A GraphQL operation that fails returns an error key.
* Requesting a statement for a period with no statement available returns its specific error key.
* That failure is recorded as a warning rather than an error.
* No GraphQL response in production includes exception details or stack traces.
* The change in the response has been agreed with the frontend team.

column1: CP - Notifications Sensitive Data
column33:
*Description* 

The notifications service records the customer's email address and their device push tokens on every notification sent. A push token is a device credential: anyone holding it can send notifications to that device. These entries are also the highest volume in the system, since the daily upcoming payments job repeats them for every customer it notifies. Logs are discarded on each deploy today, so this has to be corrected before log retention is enabled.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Notification logs identify the customer by contact id.
* No log entry contains an email address or a device push token.
* The entries written per notification are reduced to what is needed to diagnose a delivery failure.

column1: CP - Logging Verification and Findings
column33:
*Description* 

Verify the logging work already implemented against a running service instead of reviewing it as code, and sweep the eight services for sensitive information reaching the logs. The original spike was a static review scoped to shared code, so defects that only appear when the stages run together, or that live inside individual services, were out of its reach. Record each finding with its severity and decide where it is fixed, raising separate tickets for anything outside the current stages.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -The log output of a running service is reviewed for each stage already implemented.-
* -All eight services are reviewed for sensitive information in log entries.-
* -Each finding is recorded with its severity and the stage or ticket that will address it.-
* -Findings outside the scope of the current stages are raised as their own tickets.-

*Deliverables*

_Sensitive information_

* The notifications service records the customer's email address and their device push tokens on every notification sent. Raised as *CP - Notifications Sensitive Data*, to be completed before log retention is enabled.
* Unexpected GraphQL errors return the stack trace, internal endpoints and customer identifiers to the client in production. Raised as *CP - GraphQL Error Responses*.

_Missing information_

* Onboarding produces no logs of its own across its six steps, so it is not possible to tell whether a customer completed it or where they stopped. Raised as *CP - Onboarding Flow Observability*.
* The two-factor step of sign-in recorded no outcome, so the request that issues the token left no trace of which customer signed in. Addressed in Stage 4.
* Failures handled internally in the profile service record that an update failed but not for which customer. Addressed in Stage 4.

_Incorrect severity_

* A normal two-factor login was recorded as a warning, which would make any alert based on warning rates fire on healthy traffic. Addressed in Stage 4.
* Expected failures reached the logs as severe errors through the request pipeline and the GraphQL listener. Addressed in Stage 4.
* A malformed client query was recorded as a server error. Addressed in Stage 4.

_Inconsistent data_

* The customer identifier is written as a number in one entry and as text in another, so a single filter cannot match both. Addressed in Stage 4.

_Volume_

* Around 37% of each log entry is redundant: framework request fields and message placeholders already covered by the structured fields. Addressed in Stage 1.
* Every GraphQL request writes two completion entries, each with its own duration. Addressed in Stage 4.
* A single handled failure records two stack traces. Addressed in Stage 4.

_Gap in the plan_

* No alert is planned for GraphQL failures. They answer with HTTP 200, so a status-code based alarm cannot see them, and they are the only reliable signal for six of the eight services. Added to Stage 5.

_Deferred_

* Scheduled jobs produce entries with no correlation identifier and no record of each execution. The jobs already log their start, end and failures, so this is an improvement rather than a gap, and is left out of the current plan.

column1: CP - SPIKE - Investigate How Forth's "Login as Customer" Button and Email Login Link Work
column33:
*Description*

As part of the Consumer Portal replacement project, we need to review and document how Forth currently implements two customer-login mechanisms triggered from the Forth CRM:

# The *"Login as customer"* button, available to agents from a contact's Client Dashboard in Forth CRM, which logs the agent into the Consumer Portal impersonating that customer.
# The *email login link*, sent to the customer, which lets them log into the Consumer Portal without a password.

Both currently point to {{portal.cordobalegal.com?key=<token>}} / {{portal.cordobalegal.com/emaillogin?key=<token>}}. The goal of this task is to understand how this works today (token structure, validation, ownership, permissions) before deciding how — or whether — it can be carried over to our own replacement portal.

*Findings*

* Confirmed: {{DPP}} (token issuer in all links) corresponds to DebtPayPro, Forth's former product name — consistent with the CNAME target.
* Confirmed via Forth's documentation: "Login as Consumer" is gated by a role permission inside Forth CRM (Admin → Roles → Contacts → "Login as Consumer" checkbox), and is triggered from the contact's Client Dashboard.

!image-20261006-143853.png|width=458,alt="image-20261006-143853.png"!

* Investigation also surfaced two additional, related portal-access actions available on the same Contact dashboard in Forth CRM, beyond the two originally scoped: *"Change Portal Access Email"* (account administration — changes the email associated with portal access, not a login mechanism) and *"Resend Portal Welcome Email"* (see below — produces its own login link using the same underlying mechanism).

!image-20261006-150852.png|width=325,alt="image-20261006-150852.png"!

* Confirmed via Forth's end-user support articles ([https://support.forthcrm.com/hc/en-us/articles/12854485853971-Logging-into-the-Consumer-Portal-as-the-Consumer|https://support.forthcrm.com/hc/en-us/articles/12854485853971-Logging-into-the-Consumer-Portal-as-the-Consumer|smart-link] ): both login mechanisms are documented only as built-in behavior of their own hosted Consumer Portal — not as a documented integration point for external/replacement portals.
* Confirmed via Forth's documentation ([https://support.forthcrm.com/hc/en-us/articles/12854485853971-Logging-into-the-Consumer-Portal-as-the-Consumer|https://support.forthcrm.com/hc/en-us/articles/12854485853971-Logging-into-the-Consumer-Portal-as-the-Consumer|smart-link]): when an agent logs in as a consumer, the resulting session is identified as role `DRSP Agent` (matching the `role` claim found in the token) and is subject to a documented, reduced permission matrix — it does **not** inherit full customer access:

||Permission||DRSP Customer||DRSP Agent||
|canSendContactMessage|✅|❌|
|canViewDocument|✅|✅|
|canDownloadDocument|✅|❌|
|canViewStatement|❌|❌|
|canDownloadStatement|❌|❌|
|canUploadDocument|✅|❌|
|canCompleteTask|✅|❌|
|canChangePassword|✅|❌|
|canTogglePortal|✅|❌|

This confirms the impersonated session is deliberately scoped to least-privilege (mostly view-only), not equivalent to the real customer's access.

* Confirmed via Forth's public partner API docs ({{developer.setforth.com}}, full site map reviewed): there is no documented SSO/JWT/portal-login endpoint anywhere in their partner API. The only [documented auth mechanism |https://developer.setforth.com/api/get-started/authentication/get-access-token]is the existing {{client_id}}/{{client_secret}} → API key exchange we already use for the CRM REST API (contacts, debts, documents, etc.).
* Confirmed via DNS: {{client.forthpay.com}} (used by the welcome-email link, triggered via "Resend Portal Welcome Email") resolves to the same shared Forth infrastructure as {{portal.cordobalegal.com}} — both hostnames front the same multi-tenant backend, not a separate instance we could ever intervene on.
* Triggered "Resend Portal Welcome Email" on a test contact: it sends a "Welcome to FORTH" email  with a LOGIN button linking to {{<https://client.forthpay.com/emaillogin?key=<token>>}}. Decoding confirms the *same JWT scheme* as the email-login link but with a 24-hour TTL (vs. 10 minutes) and pointing to {{client.forthpay.com}}.

!image-20261006-150059.png|width=346,alt="image-20261006-150059.png"!

* *Token Comparison by Link Type:*

||Action||Route||Claims ({{data}})||TTL||Domain observed||
|Login as Customer (agent impersonation)|{{/login?key=}}|{{id}}, {{ct}} (contact_id), {{cy}}, {{at}}, {{role: DRSP Agent}}|20 min|{{portal.cordobalegal.com}}|
|Send Portal Login Link (customer magic-link)|{{/emaillogin?key=}}|{{email}}, {{contact_id}}|10 min|{{portal.cordobalegal.com}}|
|Resend Portal Welcome Email (onboarding link)|{{/emaillogin?key=}}|{{email}}, {{contact_id}}|24 h|{{client.forthpay.com}}|

All three share the same signing scheme: {{iss: DPP}}, {{aud: dpg}}, {{alg: HS256}}, plus a {{jti}} claim — confirmed only by decoding, not yet verified against Forth's signing key. Forth's own support docs independently state the 10-minute magic-link TTL, cross-validating our decoding. 

* All of these links (Login as Customer, Send Portal Login Link, Resend Portal Welcome Email) carry a {{key}} query parameter containing a JWT — three base64url-encoded parts separated by dots:
** {{header}} — algorithm used to sign it ({{alg: HS256}}, {{typ: JWT}}). Readable by anyone, no secret needed.
** {{payload}} ({{data}}) — the actual claims ({{contact_id}}, {{role}}, etc.). Also just decoded, not encrypted — anyone with the link can read it, as done throughout this investigation.
** {{signature}} — the only part that requires Forth's secret. It's what proves the token is genuine and unmodified; without verifying it, we cannot trust that a given {{key}} is real and not forged.
* Confirmed via repeated direct testing against Forth's API — "Login as Customer" tokens generated across multiple different real Forth accounts (including Daniel Pardo, Dayana Medina, Diego Giraldo, and Handersson Pacheco) and multiple different contacts:

** {{ct}} = the contact/customer ID — verified exact match against Forth's own Contact object and UI.
** {{at}} = Forth's Account ID (3821) — constant across every test, verified exact match against the {{acctID}} field on Forth User records.
** {{cy}} = the contact's own {{company_id}} field — verified exact match against the Contact object across multiple different contacts (not the triggering agent's company). In practice this has pointed to the contact's affiliate/lead-source company, not the company that services them (Cordoba Legal Group) — the exact relationship to Forth's internal {{secondary_assignments}} company types was inconsistent across contacts and isn't fully understood.
** {{id}} remains unidentified — it does not match any field on the Contact object, nor any id exposed by our own Forth integration (Debts, Transactions, Documents, Bank Account). It stays identical regardless of which account triggers the login for the same contact, and changes only when the contact changes — confirming it is tied to the contact/case, not to the individual agent.
* Hypothesis (not confirmed): because this mechanism was designed for Forth's own app to generate and validate the token, it may not have a supported path to work against a fully external, non-Forth-hosted portal — the only documented customization path found is white-labeling Forth's existing portal under our domain (custom domain + logo/colors), not replacing it outright.

*Decision Needed*

* Confirmed answer from Forth on whether these buttons ("Login as Customer", "Send Portal Login Link", "Change Portal Access Email" and "Resend Portal Welcome Email") can be reconfigured to redirect to a fully external (non-Forth-hosted) portal.
* If yes: confirmed mechanism for us to validate authenticity (signing secret dedicated to our integration, public key/JWKS, or a server-to-server verification endpoint), and confirmed/documented meaning of all token claims ({{cy}}, {{at}}, {{role}} values, single-use expectations).
* If no: a recommendation on whether to build an equivalent impersonation/quick-login feature independently (e.g., via our existing CRM API relationship) as a separate implementation ticket, scoped once this answer is known.



*Questions for Aren (Stakeholder)*

# Does Forth already know that Cordoba is building a replacement for the Consumer Portal they currently host for us?
# If Forth says they cannot reconfigure these four Customer Portal buttons (Login as Consumer, Send Portal Login Link, Change Portal Access Email, Resend Portal Welcome Email) to point to our new portal instead of their own — or takes a long time to answer — is launching the new portal without these actions working is acceptable for a first release, or is this considered launch-blocking?

*Questions for FORTH*

# Can the four Contact-dashboard actions ("Login as Customer", "Send Portal Login Link", "Change Portal Access Email", "Resend Portal Welcome Email") be reconfigured to redirect to a fully external, non-Forth-hosted portal?
# If yes, what mechanism would you provide for us to validate the authenticity of these tokens? Could you also share documentation of the token's structure and claims?
# Does the "Login as Customer" token currently carry any way to identify which individual agent triggered it? If not, could this be added?



h2. Next Steps

* Share this Spike with Aren before reaching out to Forth, since the stakeholder questions above need to be resolved first (particularly whether Forth already knows about the replacement project).
* Once that's resolved, raise the Forth questions through our existing account/integration contact, and wait for their answer.

column1: CP - Design and propose new On boarding flow to share with Aren
column33:
Message and idea: [https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1789664672586879|https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1789664672586879|smart-link] 

*On Boarding Flow Redesign*
Hey [@Aren Barge|https://cordobalegal.enterprise.slack.com/team/U08BPCRMQBU], hope you're doing well today!
Continuing from last Tuesday's meeting — kicking off a thread on the onboarding flow redesign, triggered by the duplicate-email issue we found in Forth. Below: the problem, how it works today, and three options to solve it, with pros and cons. Continue in this thread.

*On Boarding Flow Redesign*

*_Problem:_* The lack of duplicate-email verification in Forth means that, at login or onboarding time, CP has no way to reliably identify which account someone is trying to access.
*_Goal:_* Don't bring that problem into CP — the project hasn't launched yet, which is our chance to prevent it from the start and guarantee every user's email is unique in our own database.

*_How it works today (1.27.0):_*

# Login (email + password, password not validated)
# Silent redirect to onboarding if no account exists
# Confirm code — sent by email
# Create password
# Verify identity — SSN + date of birth
# Accept terms
# Done

Problems:

* The password serves no purpose and creates confusion/support calls
* An email search can resolve to the wrong account if two people share that email in Forth by mistake
* There's no duplicate detection at all.

!image (10).png|width=684,alt="image (10).png"!

*The three options*
+Before diving in: our recommendation is Option 3 below+ — it closes the same "wrong account" risk at a fraction of the cost. That said, we'd recommend reading all three, since Options 1 and 2 are what we discussed using the Account ID for last week.

*Options 1 and 2* both start from the same foundation: email is dropped as the identifier, and identity is verified with SSN + DOB as the first step, before any sensitive data is collected.

_Shared base flow_

# Login → "First time logging in?"
# Accept Terms & Privacy Policy
# Verify identity — SSN + DOB

3.1. Search Forth by SSN + DOB — 0 results: retry / 1 result: continue / 2+ results: contact us (rare case)
3.2. Check the email — already in our local system, or duplicated in Forth? +*_This is where the two options diverge._*+

# Confirm OTP — SMS, or email if there was a single result (user's choice)
# Create password
# Done

*_Option 1 — allow a secondary email_*
If there's a duplicate, the user is warned and given a choice: a secondary email just for the portal login, or contact us. Choosing a secondary email means entering it, confirming it, and confirming ownership with its own OTP (by email).
_Pros_

* The user can always get in, even with a duplicated email — fewer support calls.

_Cons_

* Reopens the work of decoupling the portal login from Forth's email.
* Most people take the fast path instead of reporting it, so Forth's data never actually gets cleaned up.
* Onboarding gets longer for anyone who sets up a secondary email — one more step, with its own OTP.

!image (11).png|width=684,alt="image (11).png"!

*_Option 2 — block and ask them to reach out_*
If there's a duplicate, there's no alternative — straight to contacting us.
_Pros_

* Forces every real duplicate to get resolved at the source — helps clean up Forth's data over time.
* Simpler to build and maintain.

_Cons_

* Anyone affected by a real duplicate is fully blocked until support resolves it — guaranteed support call.

!image (12).png|width=684,alt="image (12).png"!

*Option 3 — Keep email, fix the backend verification only*

# Login → "First time logging in?"
# Accept Terms & Privacy Policy
# Enter your email

3.1. Search Forth by that email — counts non-co-app matches instead of taking the first one

* 1 match → continues to 3.2
* 2+ matches → Contact us, account creation blocked

3.2. Check for duplicate email in our own DB

* duplicate → Contact us, account creation blocked
* clean → continues

# Confirm OTP — email (unchanged, {{ObStart}})
# Create password (unchanged, {{ObNewPassword}})
# Verify identity — SSN + DOB (unchanged, {{ObVerify}} — stays as a backstop)
# Done ({{ObCompleted}})


*Pros*

* Surgical fix — counting matches instead of taking the first one closes the "wrong account" risk, without touching anything else.
* Much cheaper — barely adds new steps, today's onboarding stays almost untouched.
* No need to touch Snowflake — email search already works through Forth's existing API; SSN + DOB would likely require it.
* Still surfaces real Forth duplicates for support to fix, same as Option 2.
* {{ObVerify}} is already a backstop if a wrong match ever slips through.

*Cons*

* A real duplicate fully blocks the user — guaranteed support call.

!image (13).png|width=684,alt="image (13).png"!



*_Decisions already made_*

* Terms & Privacy move to the front in all three options — today sensitive data is collected before the user agrees to how it's used.
* Identity verification (SSN + DOB) also moves to the front in Options 1 and 2; in Option 3 it stays exactly where it is today, as a backstop.
* For Options 1 and 2, dropped the "What's my Customer ID" lookup screen — exposing an unauthenticated SSN+DOB search is an unnecessary risk, and it's no longer needed since that's now the first step of the flow itself.
* For options 1 and 2, Email isn't used to identify anyone during onboarding because Forth's email data isn't reliable.
* How we'd resolve an already-flagged duplicate: ask the other person to update their email from their Profile (already live today); if that's too slow in practice, build an internal tool to force it later.

*The question*
In short: what do we prioritize — cost and simplicity (Option 3), fewer support calls (Option 1), or the strongest possible data-quality signal on Forth's duplicates (Option 2)?



h2. Decision / Outcome

Aren initially asked to wait for Forth's data before deciding (Slack, #software-cordobaportal, general thread with Guillermo's SQL findings). Once that data was reviewed — confirming Forth's email search returns the full set of matching contacts, which validates that counting matches in Option 3's step 1 reliably detects real duplicates — Aren confirmed agreement and gave the green light to implement *Option 3* (Slack, #software-cordobaportal, Oct 7, 2026 — [https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1791391611155979?thread_ts=1791390382.321109&cid=C0ADJS4166L).|https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1791391611155979?thread_ts=1791390382.321109&cid=C0ADJS4166L).|smart-link]

column1: CP - WEB - Documents - Align table layout, header, and mobile behavior with Transactions
column33:
*Description*

The Documents table (desktop and mobile) predates the layout work recently done on the Transactions table and doesn't share its fixes. Comparing both implementations directly surfaced several concrete gaps: no sticky header on desktop, the same mobile/desktop breakpoint bug Transactions had, and a mobile list that isn't grid-aligned — plus one issue Transactions didn't have: the document file name can be truncated with an ellipsis on narrow screens, even though it's the primary way a client identifies which document is which.

!image-20261001-144114.png|width=684,alt="image-20261001-144114.png"!

!image-20261001-150436.png|width=329,alt="image-20261001-150436.png"!

*Initial Findings*

* The desktop header doesn't stay visible while scrolling, unlike the Transactions table.
* The switch between mobile and desktop view happens at a narrower screen width than it should — the same issue found and fixed in Transactions, which caused the desktop table to overflow at in-between screen sizes.
* In the mobile view, values don't line up across rows the way they now do in Transactions.
* The document file name can be cut off with "..." on narrow screens, even though it's the main way a client identifies a document.
* A smaller layout gap found in Transactions' mobile view (that prevented content from shrinking properly) is also present here.

*Acceptance Criteria*

column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Prevent Login Lockout From Duplicate Forth Emails
column33:
h2. *Description*

Stems from [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMzEyYWVkZTM5NzQ1NDg3ODkwNzhiN2I4N2I0ODY1OTUiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMzEyYWVkZTM5NzQ1NDg3ODkwNzhiN2I4N2I0ODY1OTUiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] and [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNjIxZDI1YmViYmJlNDUxMWFmMGY0NDEyYzI1NjMzYTEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNjIxZDI1YmViYmJlNDUxMWFmMGY0NDEyYzI1NjMzYTEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link]. Login's MultipleMatches fallback resolves the local account by matching the raw email text, not ID. If two already-onboarded accounts end up sharing an email (e.g. one gets its email changed in Forth to match the other's), the account that changed is locked out of login entirely — its old email no longer resolves in Forth, and the raw-text lookup for the shared email only finds the other account.

*Current vs. Proposed Flow*

* Today: Forth reports 2+ matches → system looks up one local account by raw email text → checks password against it → fails if not found.
* Should be: Forth reports 2+ matches, with Contact IDs 
** → system looks up a local account by Contact ID for each ambiguous contact 
** → checks the password against every candidate 
** → match with no conflict syncs and logs in normally 
** → match that would conflict with a different existing account's email blocks the login and shows a "contact us" message (“We found a conflict with the email on your account. Please contact us so we can help you resolve it.“), writing nothing 
** → no match fails as invalid credentials, same as always.

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

* Login with an ambiguous email and the correct password for a non-conflicting account succeeds normally, with fresh Forth data synced.
* Login with an ambiguous email where the match would conflict with a different account fails with errorKey auth.duplicate_account_login_blocked, no data changed.
* Login with an ambiguous email where no candidate's password matches fails as invalid credentials.
* Non-conflicting fields (name, phone, SSN, dates) still sync even when the email specifically can't be.
* Submitting a wrong password against an ambiguous email does not lock out any of the other accounts that happen to share that email — only the account later confirmed as the actual match can be locked out, under the normal login rules. 
* If the matching candidate's account is already locked out, the response is the same specific "locked out" message (with wait time) as any other locked-out login attempt — not the generic invalid-credentials message.

*Deliverables*

column1: CP - SPIKE - Scope Implementation Approach for Customer Impersonation / Quick-Login
column33:
h2. Description

Following [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1891?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZDJkODZkN2E4NmEwNGFiYThmNTFmM2E4NGZkNTJlZDEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1891?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZDJkODZkN2E4NmEwNGFiYThmNTFmM2E4NGZkNTJlZDEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link], this task scopes what implementing an equivalent capability would actually require on our side, regardless of whether Forth ends up supporting an external integration or not.

The goal is not to implement anything yet, but to land the two possible paths (integrating with Forth's mechanism vs. building an independent impersonation/quick-login feature) into a concrete enough shape that the team can make an informed decision once the open dependencies are resolved — some of which are technical, and some of which depend on input from stakeholders outside engineering.

h2. Option A — Integrate with Forth

Forth agrees to let their existing "Login as Customer" and email-login buttons redirect to our own portal instead of theirs, and gives us a way to trust the tokens they issue. We'd still be the ones consuming and acting on that token — Forth doesn't hand us a finished feature, just a verified identity. This would entail:

* Validating the token (signature, {{jti}} replay protection, {{exp}}/{{nbf}}).
* Mapping {{contact_id}} to our {{ApplicationUser}}.
* Issuing our own session once the token is verified.

*Agent identity:* need Forth to confirm whether the signed token itself can expose — or be extended to expose — the identity of the agent who triggers "Login as Customer." (Already part of the Decision Needed in the [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1891?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZDJkODZkN2E4NmEwNGFiYThmNTFmM2E4NGZkNTJlZDEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1891?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZDJkODZkN2E4NmEwNGFiYThmNTFmM2E4NGZkNTJlZDEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link])

*Status:* blocked on the Forth Spike's outcome.

h2. Option B — Build it independently

Cordoba's own portal grows its own "impersonate a customer" and "passwordless login" capabilities, fully owned and controlled by us, regardless of what Forth does or doesn't support. This would entail:

* A new {{Agent}} role — reuses the existing {{ApplicationRole}}/{{UserRoles}} infrastructure and the {{AdminAuthorizeAttribute}} pattern already in the codebase.
* An admin-only panel to search a customer and trigger impersonation.
* A magic-link login, reusing the existing OTP/reset-password pattern already in {{AuthController}}.



*Agent identity/access — proposed design (not decided):*

* A bare email-domain check (eg. {{@cordobalegal.com}}/{{@hiredexperts.com}}) was explicitly rejected as insufficient authorization.
* Direction being considered: an admin-managed allowlist of individual corporate emails, modeled as {{Admin}}-managed {{ApplicationUser}} + {{Agent}} role assignments, with a new access-expiry field (e.g. {{AgentAccessExpiresAt}}) to support time-boxed access.
* Confirmed we can identify Forth agents via their Users API ({{GET /users?field[eq]=value}} resolves role to a readable name, e.g. "Agent", "Admin", "MOD Super Admin") — but haven't found a way to resolve a role into granular permissions.
* Open point: define the exact eligibility criteria for who qualifies for portal “*Support Access*“ access — which Forth role(s) qualify, restricted to our own company ({{company_id: 41402}}, excluding affiliate accounts we've seen share the same Account ID), and whether there's a reliable field to identify a Forth user's account status (e.g., `active`, {{suspended_date}}), so we don't grant access to someone who no longer has access to Forth. 
* Confirms the need for our own access-control table, where a super admin decides who gets added, rather than trusting Forth's role automatically.



*Magic-link security requirements already identified:*

* Store a hash of the token server-side, not the raw value.
* Mark it consumed at the moment of validation, not after (avoid race-condition reuse).
* Rate-limit link requests per email.
* The "request a link" endpoint must respond identically whether or not the email exists.



*Reference material:*

* Our backend contains unused scaffolding (a granular permission framework, plus {{AgentJwtFieldNames.cs}} with a {{uID}} field) that isn't wired into active code. Confluence research ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/ZgAVCw|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/ZgAVCw|smart-link] & [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/AQBbF|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/AQBbF|smart-link]) explains the likely origin: the "Agent" role was formally planned in October 2024 but explicitly deferred ("won't be supported in the nearest version") by the original team (Velvetech, no longer on the project — git history for these files was lost in a repository migration). This confirms our draft permission matrix below is original work, not duplicating a historical design.
* Confluence's "Magic Link Portal Access Module" design doc (Aug 2025, built for the AI chat assistant, not agent impersonation, [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/dwAVCw|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/dwAVCw|smart-link]) has reusable technical patterns worth referencing: RS256 signing, a revoke endpoint, and audit logging at every outcome.
* Dan Meeler proposed (2024) ([https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/kgMVCw|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/x/kgMVCw|smart-link]) that an agent shouldn't be able to open a customer's file without the customer verifying a code first — an additional design option to weigh.



h2. Applies to Both Options

*The permissions/RBAC work is required either way* — not avoided by choosing Option A, since Forth's own permission matrix applies to their portal's features, not ours. We'd still need to define what an impersonating agent can see/do across our own pages, independently of where the login mechanism comes from. A first-draft permission matrix (Customer vs. Agent) already exists, mapped to our actual portal pages — to be validated with the team, not final:

||Section / Action||Customer||Agent (proposed)||
|Dashboard (overview)|✅|✅ (view)|
|Transactions — view|✅|✅|
|Debts — view|✅|✅|
|Documents & Statements — view|✅|✅|
|Documents & Statements — download|✅|❌|
|Documents & Statements — upload|✅|❌|
|Learning Center|✅|✅ (view)|
|Support — view|✅|✅|
|Profile — view personal info|✅|✅ (view)|
|Profile — change password|✅|❌|
|Profile — bank account - view|✅|❌|
|Profile — bank account - update|✅|❌|
|Profile — update email/phone (OTP)|✅|❌|
|Notifications — view|✅|✅|
|Notifications — mark as read|✅|❌|
|Notifications — mark all as read|✅|❌|

*Is individual-agent audit traceability an actual business requirement, or an engineering best practice we're assuming matters more than it does?* This has not been confirmed with anyone who owns that decision, and it affects both paths — Option A would need Forth to add an agent-identifying claim; Option B would need the allowlist design above to carry it.

h2. Open Questions (need stakeholder input)

* Is individual-agent audit traceability a hard requirement? (see above)
* Who would operationally own managing the agent allowlist/access once built (Option B) — IT, a Cordoba admin, anyone else?

h2. Next Steps

* Confirm with Aren whether individual-agent audit traceability is a hard requirement — this materially affects the design (shared vs. per-agent account).
* Once the Forth Spike resolves whether Option A is viable, revisit this ticket to turn the relevant path into real implementation tickets — everything here is reference material to speed that up, not a commitment to build.

column1: CP - Review current Forth's CP login and onboarding flow
column33:
h2. Description

As part of understanding the Consumer Portal replacement project's starting point, this task documents how Forth's current Consumer Portal handles login and onboarding — including a duplicate-email handling gap identified during this review, discussed with the team in Slack (software-cordobaportal / general threads with Guillermo, Aren, Handersson, John, Joey).

h2. Findings

*Current flow (onboarding + login):*

_Onboarding (first time):_

# Customer enters their Account/User ID on the login page.
# Receives a one-time temporary password by email and enters it.
# Confirms identity (date of birth + last 4 SSN digits).
# Confirms the email address where they'll receive login links from now on (mandatory):
#* If that email isn't already used by another account, it's pre-filled and non-editable — they just confirm it.
#* If that email is already linked to another account, the field shows up empty instead, and the customer can type in any different email — with no check that they actually own it — and they're logged in right away with it.

_Every login after that:_

* No account number or password — the customer enters their email, receives a magic link, and clicking it logs them in.
* The account number only works once, to start onboarding — afterward, access depends entirely on email.

*Security concern:* the duplicate-email case above lets a customer claim any email as their login, with no verification that they own it (in Forth's current system, not ours).



*Real usage data (shared by Forth via SQL queries, relayed by Guillermo Malagon):*

* Total registered users on the Cordoba Legal platform: 46,197.
* Average session time: not available — Forth confirmed they cannot provide this.
* Forth's own note on {{email2}}: "rarely used, so it's quite normal for it to be empty."



*How* {{email1}}/{{email2}} actually behave: 

{{email2}} is normally identical to {{email1}} (the customer's registered email) — it only diverges specifically when a duplicate-email scenario occurs during onboarding, where it holds the alternate email the customer typed in at that step. The team initially explored this via Forth's Snowflake data warehouse, but found {{email2}} empty across the board there — likely a stale/different dataset from live ForthCRM — which is why the onboarding/login flows had to be manually emulated with test accounts to understand the real behavior (consistent with this investigation's own approach).

*Interim fix direction proposed by Guillermo (operational, not engineering):* when a customer has a duplicate email, they should call an agent to have it corrected directly in ForthCRM; the team is also working on cleaning the database toward a single source of truth.

*Alternative engineering-level fix proposed by Miguel (Option 3, agreed to by Aren in a separate thread and in this task:* [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1785?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjRlZjQ4NjA5MjUzNDYzNjlhNmM2Y2VkOGUxMTQ3ZDUiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1785?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjRlZjQ4NjA5MjUzNDYzNjlhNmM2Y2VkOGUxMTQ3ZDUiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link]*):* fix the backend verification during onboarding rather than relying on manual cleanup:

# Login → "First time logging in?" → accept Terms & Privacy.
# Enter email.
# Search Forth by that email, counting non-co-app matches instead of taking the first result:
#* 1 match → continue.
#* 2+ matches → block account creation, show "Contact us."
# Check for a duplicate email in our own DB — if duplicate, block account creation, show "Contact us"; if clean, continue.
# Confirm OTP (unchanged).
# Create password (unchanged).
# Verify identity — SSN + DOB (unchanged, stays as a backstop).
# Done.

Trade-off noted: a real duplicate fully blocks the user (guaranteed support call), but it's a surgical, low-cost fix that doesn't require touching Snowflake or redesigning the rest of onboarding.



h1. *Decision:* 

Aren confirmed agreement and gave the green light to implement Option 3 (Slack, #software-cordobaportal, Oct 7, 2026 — [https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1791391611155979?thread_ts=1791390382.321109&cid=C0ADJS4166L).|https://cordoba-legal-dev.slack.com/archives/C0ADJS4166L/p1791391611155979?thread_ts=1791390382.321109&cid=C0ADJS4166L).|smart-link]

column1: CP - Enable and validate OTP/email delivery ahead of production launch
column33:
*Description*

As part of production launch preparation, the OTP bypass that had been in place for development and testing purposes needs to be disabled, and transactional email/OTP delivery needs to be re-enabled and verified end-to-end.

While preparing this, it was identified that email delivery is currently blocked at the SendGrid account level, which would prevent OTP and other transactional emails (forgot password, email verification, etc.) from reaching users once the bypass is removed.

*Initial Findings*

* A direct request to SendGrid's API ({{POST /v3/mail/send}}) using the current API key returned an IP Access Management error: {{"The requestor's IP Address is not whitelisted"}}.

!image-20261005-151741.png|width=619,alt="image-20261005-151741.png"!

h2. Description

Companion ticket to [[https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjczZTU5MTlmY2YwNGNkMGExOWQ5YWQ0YjIyMDY3MDAiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1594?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjczZTU5MTlmY2YwNGNkMGExOWQ5YWQ0YjIyMDY3MDAiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link]].

New users currently have to enter an arbitrary password on the standard Login screen to trigger onboarding, even though that password isn't validated or used for anything. This is confusing for first-time users and generates unnecessary call center inquiries.

This adds a dedicated entry point for first-time users, reorganizes the login screen's secondary links, reorders the Terms & Privacy step within onboarding, and updates the frontend to handle the new duplicate-email responses coming from the backend fix — so genuine duplicates are communicated clearly instead of failing silently or being misrouted.

column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Fix login and onboarding account resolution against Forth
column33:
h2. *Description*

Continuing from  [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1785|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1785|smart-link] where Option 3 (keep email, fix backend verification only) was proposed and approved by Aren.

Login and onboarding both need to correctly resolve which account (if any) a given email refers to — today, several parts of that resolution are wrong. When no local account exists for an email, login silently redirects into onboarding regardless of what password was typed; this is no longer needed once a dedicated entry point exists for first-time users, and login should instead behave like a normal invalid-credentials attempt.

Separately, Forth doesn't guarantee an email is unique. Neither flow accounts for that today: the Forth lookup takes the first matching contact instead of checking whether more than one exists, and onboarding specifically resolves an account by matching the typed email against our own database before ever checking Forth — letting a second person silently land on an already-claimed local account.

Both issues live in the same account-resolution logic, so this ticket fixes them together.

h2. Current vs. Proposed Flow

h3. Login Flow

*Today:*

# User enters email + password.
# System asks Forth for that email first (login already does this correctly, unlike onboarding).
# Forth returns the first match it finds, without checking if there's more than one.
# System looks up the local account using that match's real identity.
# If a local account exists, continues the login normally.
# If no local account exists, the system automatically redirects into onboarding — regardless of the password entered.

*Should be:*

# User enters email + password.
# System asks Forth for that email.
# Forth counts how many people match:
#* None → login fails: *"Username or password is incorrect"* _(existing message, unchanged)_
#* More than one → login fails with that same message
#* Exactly one → continues
# If no local account exists for that match, login fails with that same message _(the dedicated "first time logging in?" entry point handles new users instead — no more auto-redirect)_.
# If a local account exists but hasn't finished onboarding, it resumes onboarding as today (unchanged).
# If a local account exists and onboarding is complete, it continues the login normally.

h3. Onboarding Flow

*Today:*

# User enters their email to start registration.
# System first checks our own database for an existing account with that email.
# If found, continues with that account — without checking anything further in Forth.
# Only if no local match is found does it ask Forth.
# If Forth finds no one, registration fails with "Customer not found" (unchanged today and going forward).
# If Forth returns several people with that email, the system keeps the first one, without flagging it.
# With that person (right or wrong), creates the account and continues.

*Should be:*

# User enters their email to start registration.
# System asks Forth first, not our own database.
# Forth counts how many people match:
#* None → *"Customer not found"* _(existing message, unchanged)_
#* More than one → *"We found more than one account matching that information. Please contact us so we can help you get set up."* _(new)_, stops there
#* Exactly one → continues with that person
# Checks our own database for an existing account using that person's real identity, not the email text.
# If they already have an account, continues with that one.
# If not, checks whether the email is already used by someone else before creating a new account:
#* Yes → *"The email address '{email}' is already linked to another account. Please contact us so we can help you get set up."* _(new)_, stops there
#* No → creates the account and registration continues as normal.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -Logging in with an email that has no local account fails the same way as invalid credentials, regardless of the password entered.-
* -Logging in with an email that has a local account but hasn't completed onboarding fails the same way as invalid credentials. Resuming an incomplete onboarding is handled exclusively through the dedicated entry point ("Is this your first login?"), not through the standard Login form.-
* -Logging in with an email matching more than one Forth contact fails the same way as if the email didn't exist.-
* -Starting registration with an email matching more than one Forth contact shows a "contact us" message and does not create an account.-
* -Starting registration resolves the account using Forth's match first, then checks locally by that identity — not by the raw email text.-
* -Starting registration with an email that resolves to one Forth contact, but is already used by a different local account, shows a "contact us" message and does not create a second account.-
* -Existing behavior for a correctly resolved, non-duplicated, already-onboarded account is unchanged in both flows.-

h2. Pending Task

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Unit test for auth and on boarding flow*

It would be worth creating automated tests for the authentication module as a whole, not just for this fix. Right now this area has no test coverage, and tests would help prevent similar issues from reaching production in the future.

Proposed as a separate follow-up ticket: [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZjFkYmM1NmY0NTQ3NDE0Yjg0YmUwYTcwYTA2YmI0YTQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1930?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZjFkYmM1NmY0NTQ3NDE0Yjg0YmUwYTcwYTA2YmI0YTQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] 

Will check with [~accountid:712020:313307ce-3202-4da7-b5a3-adcbee32f188] and [~accountid:712020:bba04ff1-46ba-4373-b0a0-5581ead637b3] for approval before moving forward with this.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Given how much nuance these account-resolution flows carry, they'll be documented in more detail in a dedicated Confluence page as a follow-up task: [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1854?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMTliNWEzMzM3NTAzNGI5MzgxNDAxOTEyOTA1MDAyZGYiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1854?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMTliNWEzMzM3NTAzNGI5MzgxNDAxOTEyOTA1MDAyZGYiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link].
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Known weak point, not addressed in this ticket*

{{/auth/onboarding/start}} has no rate limiting. Its response reveals whether an email exists in Forth and whether it's duplicated, and a "found" result sends a real OTP — so it can be used to enumerate customer emails and spam inboxes.

Proposed as a separate follow-up: [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1935?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjc4MjJiZDlmMTA4NDM5ZjkxMjgwM2JmOTkxOWFkYWEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1935?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjc4MjJiZDlmMTA4NDM5ZjkxMjgwM2JmOTkxOWFkYWEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] 
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Known weak point, not addressed in this ticket*

Login's MultipleMatches fallback resolves the account by raw email text, not ID. If two already-onboarded accounts end up sharing an email (e.g. one changes its Forth email to match the other's), the account that changed gets locked out of login entirely.

Proposed as a separate follow-up: [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1938?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiOTllYmZiMGMwYzY3NDNmYmFiMTBkZDlmMDk0ZTM0ODgiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1938?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiOTllYmZiMGMwYzY3NDNmYmFiMTBkZDlmMDk0ZTM0ODgiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] 
{panel}

h2. Deliverables

[https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/196|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-backend/pull/196|smart-link] 

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Three refinements added during testing, beyond the original design:*

* On boarding: If no Forth match is found for the submitted email, but a local account still has that exact email stored from before it changed in Forth, that account gets refreshed against its own current Forth data in the background — so a later attempt with the real, current email works cleanly, without needing anyone to intervene.
* *On login:* When Forth returns more than one match for an email (an ambiguous, duplicated email on Forth's side), login no longer blocks outright. If a local account already exists for that email and the submitted password is correct for it, the user logs in normally — their identity is already uniquely established locally, regardless of what Forth shows.

*Additional finding (found during frontend work, fixed in this ticket)*

{{AcceptTermsAsync}} (Agreement step) was marking {{OnBoardingCompleted = true}} right when Terms were accepted — correct only while Agreement was the last step. Once the frontend moved Agreement to right after OTP confirmation (before password + identity verification), this would mark accounts as fully onboarded before they'd set a password or verified identity, breaking login and blocking retries.

Fix: moved {{OnBoardingCompleted = true}} and the FCM-token association from {{AcceptTermsAsync}} to {{ConfirmIdentityAsync}} (the real last step). No frontend change needed — {{fcmToken}} is mobile-only, and the web client's navigation never depended on the returned status.
{panel}

*1. Onboarding - Start (no match on Forth)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms a completely unknown email is rejected cleanly, unchanged from today. 
* _Setup:_ use an email that doesn't exist in Forth at all. 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.customer_not_found}}.

!image-20261009-203811.png|width=684,alt="image-20261009-203811.png"!

*2. Onboarding - Start (2+ matches on Forth)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms the core fix — a duplicated email in Forth blocks account creation instead of silently picking one. 
* _Setup:_ a Forth email shared by 2+ non-co-applicant contacts. 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.multiple_customers_found}}. No local account gets created.

!image-20261009-204314.png|width=684,alt="image-20261009-204314.png"!

# *Onboarding - Start (1 match, no CP account yet)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms the normal, happy-path signup still works. 
* _Setup:_ a Forth contact with a unique email and no existing local account. 
* _Expected:_ {{TwoFactorRequired}} (OTP sent), and a new local account is created tied to that contact.

!image-20261009-182122.png|width=684,alt="image-20261009-182122.png"!

*4. Onboarding - Start (already onboarded)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms someone who already finished onboarding can't start it again. 
* _Setup:_ use the email of an account that already completed onboarding. 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.already_onboarded}}.

!image-20261009-204723.png|width=684,alt="image-20261009-204723.png"!

*5. Email claimed due to stale sync (now self-resolves)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms the self-healing resync — a conflict caused by the other account's Forth email simply having changed resolves on its own. 
* _Setup:_ Account A completes onboarding with {{stale@outlook.com}} (Contact ID 100). In Forth, change Contact 100's email to something else. From CP, assign {{stale@outlook.com}} to a different contact (Contact ID 200, no local account). 
* _Expected:_ {{TwoFactorRequired}} — a new account gets created for Contact ID 200. No {{email_already_registered}} error; the resync frees up the email automatically.

!image-20261009-211700.png|width=684,alt="image-20261009-211700.png"!

*6. Onboarding - Confirm (OTP)* 

* _Purpose:_ regression check — confirms the step right after a successful Start still works unchanged. 
* _Setup:_ use the OTP returned by test case 3. 
* _Expected:_ succeeds, returns the onboarding access token.

!image-20261013-134954.png|width=684,alt="image-20261013-134954.png"!

!image-20261013-135009.png|width=684,alt="image-20261013-135009.png"!

*7. Login - Password Sign In (regression)* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms a brand-new email (no account anywhere) no longer auto-redirects into onboarding — it just fails like a normal wrong login. 
* _Setup:_ an email with no local account and no Forth match (or a valid Forth match with no local account). 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.invalid_credentials}} — never {{OnboardingRequiredVia2FA}}.

!image-20261013-144818.png|width=684,alt="image-20261013-144818.png"!

*8. Login - started onboarding but never finished*

* Purpose: confirms Login never resumes onboarding on its own, even for an account that already exists but hasn't finished.
* Setup: an account that exists locally but hasn't completed onboarding.
* Expected: Failed, {{errorKey: auth.invalid_credentials}} — never OnboardingRequiredVia2FA.

*9a. Onboarding - Start, already onboarded, tries again* 

* _Purpose:_ same intent as test 4, confirming it also holds after the reorder (Forth-first resolution) — not just before it. 
* _Setup:_ same as test 4. 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.already_onboarded}}.

!image-20261013-150017.png|width=684,alt="image-20261013-150017.png"!

*9b. Already onboarded — confirms the sync still happens* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms that even when blocked by {{already_onboarded}}, the local record gets refreshed with the latest Forth data before responding. 
* _Setup:_ same type of account as test 9a (already onboarded), but first change that contact's email in Forth to a new one, then call Start endpoint with that new email. 
* _Expected:_ {{Failed}}, {{errorKey: auth.already_onboarded}} — and, checking the database, that account's local email has already been updated to the new one.

!Screen Recording 2026-10-13 at 10.07.14 AM.mov|width=684,alt="Screen Recording 2026-10-13 at 10.07.14 AM.mov"!

*10. Login with an email that has 2+ matches on Forth, with a local account already existing* 

* _Purpose:_ confirms the final refinement — a legitimate existing user isn't locked out just because Forth later became ambiguous for their email; login falls back to the local account and succeeds with the right password. 
* _Setup:_ a Forth email shared by 2+ contacts, where one of them already has a completed local account. 
* _Expected:_ with the correct password, login succeeds normally. With a wrong password, fails as invalid credentials — same as any other wrong-password attempt.

!Screen Recording 2026-10-13 at 10.23.57 AM.mov|width=684,alt="Screen Recording 2026-10-13 at 10.23.57 AM.mov"!

column1: CX - Backend - Error message in login
column33:
h2. Description

CreditorX Android and iOS customers are currently seeing a generic *“Error”* message when attempting to log in with valid credentials. This message does not explain the root cause or provide enough information to reproduce or diagnose the problem.

Previous research by [~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] indicates that the generic error appears when the Kazoo login flow fails. The issue only occurs when the customer’s login credentials are valid. When credentials are invalid, the client correctly returns the message *“User not found or incorrect”*.

Additional investigation is needed to identify why Kazoo fails during valid login attempts, improve observability around the failure, and return a clearer error message to the customer when this scenario occurs.

[~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] also noted that, during each login attempt, the system changes the password in Kazoo because the Kazoo user password is required to authenticate against the Kazoo API. Since Kazoo does not provide an endpoint to retrieve the current password, the system creates a new password during each login attempt to know the active password.

!!!!But saying it's because of Kazoo is just a guess; with this error message, it's impossible to determine if Kazoo is the cause. Part of this task is figuring out what's causing the login to fail.

!image-20261005-195050.png|width=203,alt="image-20261005-195050.png"!

* -The backend logs enough diagnostic information to identify when a valid login fails because of a Kazoo authentication or password update issue.-

column33:

[https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/requestreviewaction|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/requestreviewaction|smart-link] 

+After a customer logs+ in to the iOS app, display an in-app popup inviting them to rate and review the app using the native App Store in-app review flow. The experience should open the App Store rating and review modal inside the app, without redirecting the customer to the App Store app.

The popup should appear at an appropriate moment immediately after login, avoid interrupting critical user actions, and gracefully handle cases where the App Store review flow is unavailable or dismissed by the customer.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Given a customer successfully logs in to the iOS app, when the post-login experience loads, then the app shows a popup inviting the customer to rate and review the app.

* Given the customer chooses to leave a rating or review, when the popup action is selected, then the native App Store in-app review modal opens within the app without redirecting to the App Store app.

* Given the App Store review modal is unavailable, fails to load, or is dismissed, when the flow ends, then the app handles the outcome gracefully without blocking login or app usage.

* Given the popup has been shown or completed according to the configured display rules, when the same customer logs in again, then the app does not show the popup repeatedly in a disruptive way. (every 90 days the app will ask for the rating again if he has never rate the app)
* Given the feature is implemented, when it is tested on supported iOS versions and App Store review configurations, then the rating and review flow behaves consistently and does not introduce login regressions.

01/Sep/26 10:24 AM;712020:fd36cadf-9806-42d0-93a9-02002d8431e5;[~accountid:712020:313307ce-3202-4da7-b5a3-adcbee32f188] 

Moving this to Blocked.

While investigating this ticket I traced the call flow end-to-end: {{KazooController::handle()}} ({{app/Http/Controllers/Kazoo/KazooController.php}}) is invoked by Kazoo via {{POST /kazoo/number/handle}}, and it decides {{is_caller_known}} based on {{block_collectors}} and the creditor/blocked-phone tables. On the Kazoo side, the callflow this app provisions per account ({{KazooAPIClient::createCallFlow}}, see the {{is_lawyer_required}} module in {{app/Integrations/KazooAPIClient.php}}) matches a live custom Erlang module I found on the telephony server ({{cf_is_lawyer_required.beam}} on {{logic1}}). I decompiled it and confirmed it only reads a custom channel variable ({{Is-Creditor}}) to decide the branch — it does not call our backend directly.

I need to find where that {{Is-Creditor}} variable actually gets set (i.e., whatever component makes the real HTTP call to {{/kazoo/number/handle}}), since that's outside this repo. I've ruled out FreeSWITCH ({{fs1}}) as the source — no custom Lua/{{mod_xml_curl}}/dialplan curl logic is loaded there, only stock {{mod_kazoo}} — and there's no matching source tree on {{logic1}} either (the {{compile_info}} in the beam file points to {{/usr/local/src/applications/callflow/src/module/cf_is_lawyer_required.erl}}, which doesn't exist on that server).

Based on the CBMA Confluence documentation, the custom Kazoo/Erlang code lives in a separate repository ({{gitlab.velvetech.com/forth-new/cordoba/kazoo}}) that I don't currently have access to. I need access to that repo to locate the actual source for {{cf_is_lawyer_required}} and whatever module sets {{Is-Creditor}}, so I can confirm the real end-to-end flow and safely make changes here without breaking the Kazoo-side integration.

Could someone grant me access, or point me to who owns/maintains that repo?

column1: CX - Android - Implement redirect to Google play for rating the app
column33:
Currently, there is no reliable way to determine whether the in-app rating popup was actually shown to the customer. To avoid false assumptions about popup visibility, we need to replace the current in-app review prompt with a direct redirect to the app listing in Google Play, where customers can leave their rating.

This change should ensure the Android rating flow is predictable, measurable, and avoids relying on the system-controlled in-app review popup behavior.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -The Android app no longer triggers the native in-app review popup for the rating flow.-
* -When the customer chooses to rate the app, they are redirected to the app listing in Google Play.-
* -If Google Play is not available on the device, the app handles the scenario gracefully without crashing.-
* -The rating flow behavior is documented or logged so the team can confirm that the redirect was initiated.-
* -The updated flow is validated on supported Android versions and does not introduce regressions in the existing customer experience.-

08/Oct/26 10:32 AM;712020:dac1dce4-8aa1-4b7e-8cd4-12205fb8c6e4;After an extensive investigation, we found that we can't reliably build a fallback for when the customer doesn't see the rating window. Google's In-App Review API doesn't tell the app whether the window was shown or whether the customer left a rating ([Google docs|https://developer.android.com/guide/playcore/in-app-review/kotlin-java]), so we can't detect when to fall back.

The feature itself works: [~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27]  tested it on a new device, and the Google Play rating window appeared as expected. When it doesn't appear, it's because Google limits how often it shows the window to the same user.

*My suggestion*: if we want to make sure customers can always rate the app, the "Rate the app" button should send them to our Google Play Store page instead. That's what Google recommends for a rating button ([Google docs|https://developer.android.com/guide/playcore/in-app-review#quotas]). We'd keep the same rules we already have: a 90-day cooldown between prompts and at most 3 prompts per customer. [~accountid:712020:313307ce-3202-4da7-b5a3-adcbee32f188]

* -Dashboard created in CloudWatch-

column1: CX - Database uses update and check for admin
column33:
Summary

Update the {{admin}} user's password in the database and use the new password to update the backend, then check if the Admin is working perfectly

h3. Context

This work affects the Back Apps and the manual backup process. It is also related to verifying that admin access still works after the password change.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Update the {{admin}} user's password in the database.
* Update the backend with the new password.
* Create a user in admin for the person who will perform the password update, so they can verify access still works after the change.
* Change the password.
* Verify the full functionality in Admin.
* Enable MySQL command logs.

h3. Other information

* This affects:
** Back Apps
** BackUp Manual
* 2.1 and 2.2 are listed in the original description.
